definition: Incontrovertible evidence refers to evidence that leaves no doubt as to a particular conclusion. It is the evidence introduced to prove a fact in a trial which is supposed to be so conclusive that there can be no other truth as to the matter. Examples might include a fingerprint showing that someone was present in a room, or a blood test proving who parented a child.
